ca_columbia_bouldering.blurb: Columbia Bouldering is a spread of boulders in and around the town of Columbia, near Sonora, California, scattered through oak woodland and manzanita around Columbia State Historic Park, with more on the Columbia College campus. It is all bouldering. The problems favour pockets, crimps, tufas and sharp edges rather than slopers or friction, and grades run from V0 to V8 with a few harder, the V1 to V4 range being best represented. The Labyrinth holds the most problems, followed by Columbia State Historic Park, Lower Arboretum and Upper Arboretum. It can be climbed year-round, but fall and winter are the best, when cooler days help; in summer early mornings or evenings are the workable hours.

ca_e_yosemite_falls_area.blurb: Yosemite Falls Area lies on the north side of Yosemite Valley, below a waterfall counted among the highest in the world. Trad climbing dominates, with a good number of boulder problems and a few sport, top-rope and aid lines. Roped grades run from 5.5 to 5.11, clustering around 5.10, while the boulder problems are mostly at the easy end. Swan Slab, across from Yosemite Lodge, is a popular cliff with many moderate trad routes. Sunnyside Bench, Lower Falls Amphitheater and Five Open Books add more multi-pitch and crack climbing, and Lost Arrow Spire on the Upper Falls Wall has longer, committing lines, with several grade VI routes in the area.

ca_mill_creek_road_area.blurb: Mill Creek Road Area covers the crags south of Highway 18 above Big Bear Lake, in the San Bernardino Mountains of Southern California. About half the climbs are boulder problems, mostly at the easy end of the V scale, with Snow Summit Boulders the largest group and Little Tibet, on Bluff Mesa, adding granite boulders scattered across the mesa. Roped climbing centres on Black Bluff, a remote granite crag of mostly crack climbs on its north and west faces, where trad dominates. Rope grades run from 5.5 to 5.12, with most at 5.10. Siberia Creek and Arctic Temple add smaller options, and a few routes here are tagged alpine in character.

ky_crp_cliffview_recreational_preserve.blurb: Cliffview Recreational Preserve is a recently developed climbing area in the southern part of Red River Gorge, near Campton, Kentucky, with more than thirty cliff faces strung along about three and a half miles of cliff line. Sport climbing makes up most of the routes, with a smaller amount of trad and a few boulder problems. Grades start around 5.6 and top out near 5.13, with the weight on 5.10 through 5.12. The routes sit in several clusters: The Fed is the largest, followed by 19th Hole, Pirates' Cove and Mosh Pit. Because the routes are new, holds can still break, so helmets for both climber and belayer are a sensible precaution.

nh_wm_kinsman_notch.blurb: Kinsman Notch is a pass in the White Mountains of New Hampshire that holds a mix of climbing styles. About half the climbs are boulder problems, notably the Beast Area Bouldering and Kinsman Notch East, with problems from V0 into the V8 range. The Lost River Crags are mostly trad, with some sport and a little bouldering, in grades from 5.5 into the 5.10s. The Notch is best known for ice and mixed: the heavily wooded Kinsman Notch Ice crag, also called Luck O' The Irish, holds routes from WI2 to WI5 and mixed lines up to the M9 range, shaded from the sun and sheltered from wind. Rock grades overall run from 5.6 to 5.12, mostly 5.9 and 5.10.

ut_blacksmith_fork_canyon.blurb: Blacksmith Fork Canyon is a quiet limestone canyon above Hyrum, in Cache Valley in the northern Wasatch of Utah. Sport climbing dominates, with a block of boulder problems and only a little trad. Grades run from 5.6 to 5.13, and the heaviest concentration is in the 5.11 to 5.13 range, though there are enough easier routes to suit moderate climbers. Left Hand Fork holds the most climbs, including Hardware Wall, a shady crag where most routes are around mid-5.12. At the canyon mouth, Sea Wall is a limestone cliff band with an unusually dense set of easy to moderate sport routes; the rock there is chossy, so helmets and care are needed. Other smaller walls include The Little Prints Wall and Grass Marsh Higgledy Pig.
